    Showcase — the 2023 Canadian wildfires (FIRMS + Sentinel-2 dNBR)¶

    2023 was Canada's worst fire season on record: about 10–14 million hectares burned — roughly 4.7× the 1986–2022 average. This notebook combines two earthlens backends: NASA FIRMS active-fire detections (where and how intensely things were burning, day by day) and Sentinel-2 via GEE to map post-fire burn severity with the standard dNBR index.

    What this notebook does¶

    1. FIRMS — pull a week of VIIRS active-fire detections over Quebec at the peak.
    2. Map them by fire radiative power (FRP) and count detections per day.
    3. FRP distribution — how intense were the fires?
    4. dNBR burn severity — compare Sentinel-2 before/after, classify severity, and estimate burned area per class.

    Needs FIRMS_MAP_KEY (free) for the FIRMS cells and GEE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT / GEE_SERVICE_KEY for the Sentinel-2 cells; each part skips gracefully if its credentials are absent.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import os, tempfile, base64
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from loguru import logger
from earthlens import EarthLens
from pyramids.dataset import Dataset

logger.disable("earthlens"); logger.disable("pyramids")
SERVICE_ACCOUNT = os.environ.get("GEE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT", "my-sa@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com")
SERVICE_KEY = os.environ.get("GEE_SERVICE_KEY", "/path/to/key.json")

def grab(collection, aoi, start, end, bands, scale, reducer="median"):
    """Download one GEE composite over [start,end]; return GeoTIFF path or None.
    aoi = [lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max]."""
    el = EarthLens(
        data_source="gee", start=start, end=end, temporal_resolution="raw",
        variables={collection: list(bands)},
        lat_lim=[aoi[1], aoi[3]], lon_lim=[aoi[0], aoi[2]],
        path=tempfile.mkdtemp(), scale=scale, reducer=reducer,
        service_account=SERVICE_ACCOUNT, service_key=SERVICE_KEY,
    )
    try:
        p = el.download(progress_bar=False)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        print("download skipped (needs GEE credentials):", exc); return None
    return str(p[0]) if p else None

def read(path):
    return np.asarray(Dataset.read_file(str(path)).read_array(), dtype="float32")

# --- FIRMS: a week of VIIRS active-fire detections over Quebec, Jun 2023 ---
# VIIRS_SNPP_SP is the archive product (historical dates); each row is one fire pixel.
fires = None
if os.environ.get("FIRMS_MAP_KEY"):
    try:
        fires = EarthLens(data_source="firms", variables=["VIIRS_SNPP_SP"],
            start="2023-06-02", end="2023-06-08", lat_lim=[48.0, 53.0], lon_lim=[-80.0, -72.0],
            path=tempfile.mkdtemp()).download(progress_bar=False)
        print(f"{len(fires):,} fire detections")
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        print("skipped FIRMS query:", exc)
else:
    print("set FIRMS_MAP_KEY to run the FIRMS cells")
    import os, tempfile, base64 import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt from loguru import logger from earthlens import EarthLens from pyramids.dataset import Dataset logger.disable("earthlens"); logger.disable("pyramids") SERVICE_ACCOUNT = os.environ.get("GEE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT", "my-sa@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com") SERVICE_KEY = os.environ.get("GEE_SERVICE_KEY", "/path/to/key.json") def grab(collection, aoi, start, end, bands, scale, reducer="median"): """Download one GEE composite over [start,end]; return GeoTIFF path or None. aoi = [lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max].""" el = EarthLens( data_source="gee", start=start, end=end, temporal_resolution="raw", variables={collection: list(bands)}, lat_lim=[aoi[1], aoi[3]], lon_lim=[aoi[0], aoi[2]], path=tempfile.mkdtemp(), scale=scale, reducer=reducer, service_account=SERVICE_ACCOUNT, service_key=SERVICE_KEY, ) try: p = el.download(progress_bar=False) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 print("download skipped (needs GEE credentials):", exc); return None return str(p[0]) if p else None def read(path): return np.asarray(Dataset.read_file(str(path)).read_array(), dtype="float32") # --- FIRMS: a week of VIIRS active-fire detections over Quebec, Jun 2023 --- # VIIRS_SNPP_SP is the archive product (historical dates); each row is one fire pixel. fires = None if os.environ.get("FIRMS_MAP_KEY"): try: fires = EarthLens(data_source="firms", variables=["VIIRS_SNPP_SP"], start="2023-06-02", end="2023-06-08", lat_lim=[48.0, 53.0], lon_lim=[-80.0, -72.0], path=tempfile.mkdtemp()).download(progress_bar=False) print(f"{len(fires):,} fire detections") except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 print("skipped FIRMS query:", exc) else: print("set FIRMS_MAP_KEY to run the FIRMS cells")
    24,702 fire detections

    Where and how intensely — the active-fire map¶

    Copied! 
    # Each detection at its lon/lat, coloured by log(FRP) (fire radiative power, MW).
if fires is not None and len(fires):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 7))
    sc = ax.scatter(fires.longitude, fires.latitude, c=np.log10(fires.frp.clip(lower=1)),
                    cmap="inferno", s=6, alpha=0.6)
    ax.set(xlabel="longitude", ylabel="latitude",
           title=f"Quebec — VIIRS active fire, 2–8 Jun 2023 ({len(fires):,} detections)")
    fig.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, label="log10 FRP (MW)"); plt.show()
    # Each detection at its lon/lat, coloured by log(FRP) (fire radiative power, MW). if fires is not None and len(fires): fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 7)) sc = ax.scatter(fires.longitude, fires.latitude, c=np.log10(fires.frp.clip(lower=1)), cmap="inferno", s=6, alpha=0.6) ax.set(xlabel="longitude", ylabel="latitude", title=f"Quebec — VIIRS active fire, 2–8 Jun 2023 ({len(fires):,} detections)") fig.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, label="log10 FRP (MW)"); plt.show()

    How intense — the FRP distribution¶

    Fire radiative power (FRP) measures the energy a fire is emitting. A heavy tail towards high FRP marks the most intense, fast-spreading fire fronts.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    # Histogram of FRP (log-x) plus the total radiative power of the scene.
if fires is not None and len(fires):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.4))
    ax.hist(fires.frp.clip(lower=1), bins=np.logspace(0, 3.5, 40), color="darkorange")
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set(xlabel="FRP (MW, log scale)", ylabel="detections",
           title="Fire radiative power distribution"); plt.show()
    print(f"median FRP {fires.frp.median():.1f} MW | total {fires.frp.sum()/1e3:.1f} GW across {len(fires):,} pixels")
    # Histogram of FRP (log-x) plus the total radiative power of the scene. if fires is not None and len(fires): fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.4)) ax.hist(fires.frp.clip(lower=1), bins=np.logspace(0, 3.5, 40), color="darkorange") ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set(xlabel="FRP (MW, log scale)", ylabel="detections", title="Fire radiative power distribution"); plt.show() print(f"median FRP {fires.frp.median():.1f} MW | total {fires.frp.sum()/1e3:.1f} GW across {len(fires):,} pixels")
    median FRP 7.3 MW | total 517.8 GW across 24,702 pixels

    Burn severity from Sentinel-2 (dNBR)¶

    After a fire, the Normalized Burn Ratio NBR = (NIR − SWIR) / (NIR + SWIR) drops sharply (healthy vegetation is bright in NIR B8, char is bright in SWIR B12). The differenced NBR, dNBR = NBR_before − NBR_after, is the standard burn-severity index. We compare a pre-season (May) and post-season (September) Sentinel-2 composite over one burned area and classify severity with the USGS thresholds.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    # Pre/post Sentinel-2 NBR over one burned area -> dNBR -> USGS severity classes.
BURN_AOI = [-77.0, 51.0, -76.0, 52.0]   # a dense Quebec burn (1 deg box)
def nbr(start, end):
    p = grab("COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED", BURN_AOI, start, end, ["B8", "B12"], scale=80)
    if not p: return None
    a = read(p); return (a[0] - a[1]) / (a[0] + a[1] + 1e-6)
nbr_pre, nbr_post = nbr("2023-05-01", "2023-05-31"), nbr("2023-09-01", "2023-09-30")
if nbr_pre is not None and nbr_post is not None:
    h, w = min(nbr_pre.shape[0], nbr_post.shape[0]), min(nbr_pre.shape[1], nbr_post.shape[1])
    dnbr = nbr_pre[:h, :w] - nbr_post[:h, :w]
    # USGS dNBR severity thresholds
    bounds = [-0.1, 0.1, 0.27, 0.44, 0.66, 1.3]
    names = ["unburned", "low", "moderate-low", "moderate-high", "high"]
    px_km2 = (80 * 80) / 1e6
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))
    im = ax[0].imshow(dnbr, cmap="RdYlGn_r", vmin=-0.1, vmax=1.0)
    ax[0].set_title("dNBR burn severity"); ax[0].axis("off")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax[0], fraction=0.046, label="dNBR")
    areas = [np.sum((dnbr >= bounds[i]) & (dnbr < bounds[i + 1])) * px_km2 for i in range(5)]
    ax[1].bar(names, areas, color=["#2c7bb6","#abd9e9","#ffffbf","#fdae61","#d7191c"])
    ax[1].set_ylabel("area (km^2)"); ax[1].set_title("Area by burn-severity class")
    plt.setp(ax[1].get_xticklabels(), rotation=30, ha="right"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
    burned = sum(areas[1:])
    print(f"burned area in this 1-deg tile: {burned:,.0f} km^2 "
          f"({areas[3]+areas[4]:,.0f} km^2 moderate-high to high severity)")
else:
    print("Sentinel-2 dNBR skipped — set GEE credentials and rerun")
    # Pre/post Sentinel-2 NBR over one burned area -> dNBR -> USGS severity classes. BURN_AOI = [-77.0, 51.0, -76.0, 52.0] # a dense Quebec burn (1 deg box) def nbr(start, end): p = grab("COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED", BURN_AOI, start, end, ["B8", "B12"], scale=80) if not p: return None a = read(p); return (a[0] - a[1]) / (a[0] + a[1] + 1e-6) nbr_pre, nbr_post = nbr("2023-05-01", "2023-05-31"), nbr("2023-09-01", "2023-09-30") if nbr_pre is not None and nbr_post is not None: h, w = min(nbr_pre.shape[0], nbr_post.shape[0]), min(nbr_pre.shape[1], nbr_post.shape[1]) dnbr = nbr_pre[:h, :w] - nbr_post[:h, :w] # USGS dNBR severity thresholds bounds = [-0.1, 0.1, 0.27, 0.44, 0.66, 1.3] names = ["unburned", "low", "moderate-low", "moderate-high", "high"] px_km2 = (80 * 80) / 1e6 fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5)) im = ax[0].imshow(dnbr, cmap="RdYlGn_r", vmin=-0.1, vmax=1.0) ax[0].set_title("dNBR burn severity"); ax[0].axis("off") fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax[0], fraction=0.046, label="dNBR") areas = [np.sum((dnbr >= bounds[i]) & (dnbr < bounds[i + 1])) * px_km2 for i in range(5)] ax[1].bar(names, areas, color=["#2c7bb6","#abd9e9","#ffffbf","#fdae61","#d7191c"]) ax[1].set_ylabel("area (km^2)"); ax[1].set_title("Area by burn-severity class") plt.setp(ax[1].get_xticklabels(), rotation=30, ha="right"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show() burned = sum(areas[1:]) print(f"burned area in this 1-deg tile: {burned:,.0f} km^2 " f"({areas[3]+areas[4]:,.0f} km^2 moderate-high to high severity)") else: print("Sentinel-2 dNBR skipped — set GEE credentials and rerun")
    burned area in this 1-deg tile: 4,906 km^2 (122 km^2 moderate-high to high severity)

    Recap¶

    Two backends, two complementary views: FIRMS shows the fire while it burns (location, timing, intensity), and Sentinel-2 dNBR measures the lasting damage afterwards by severity class — the standard pre/post burn-severity workflow.

    Try it yourself¶

    • Move BURN_AOI over a different fire complex, or widen the FIRMS box.
    • Swap VIIRS_SNPP_SP for MODIS_SP, or compute RdNBR (relativised dNBR).
    • See the FIRMS and GEE backend references.
